text:
caroline: Hey team, hitting a weird failure on the quickstart — first API call from the Node sample returns a 502 from our proxy and the SDK just retries a few times then errors. No app code changed.

caroline: curl -v http://api.redwood.example/v1/chat -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -d '{"input":"hi"}'
* result: *
*  HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
*  server: redwood-proxy
*  content-type: text/html

raj: can you paste the full verbose output (including headers) and the SDK version?

caroline: SDK 1.8.2, verbose shows a 302 redirect to https://console.redwood.example/onboarding/payments before the 502. Looks like proxy tried to follow but failed.

maya: this rings a bell — we had an onboarding flow where new workspaces that haven't accepted billing/terms get redirected to the payments page. The proxy isn't following the redirect in some cases and ends up returning 502 to the client. Not the best UX.

morgan: @caroline can you confirm if the workspace has a billing method or accepted the org TOS? Also did you sign up via invite or SSO?

caroline: invite. I never finished the billing step; assumed quickstart would still allow test calls with free credits.

raj: that explains it. The redirect -> proxy mismatch produces 502 instead of a clear 402/403 in the SDK. Workaround: finish the billing/accept TOS in console or use a personal dev workspace token that already has billing.

caroline: confirmed — added a card and accepted TOS, retried the Node sample and first call succeeded. Thanks.

maya: filing a bug so SDK maps this case to a clearer error instead of surfacing a proxy 502. Proposed: detect redirect to onboarding/payment and return an SDK error like "Workspace requires billing/terms: ACTION_REQUIRED" with link to console.

devex-bot: created ticket DX-7421: "quickstart: proxy 502 when workspace requires billing redirect" assigned to eng-platform.

raj: also adding a short note to the onboarding quickstart README to mention the billing acceptance step and to surface the console link in the sample error handler.

caroline: can we also get a friendlier cloud error in the hosted API logs? Right now customers see 502 and think the service is down.

morgan: agreed — I'll loop in eng-sre to add clearer log classification and maybe a metric to detect how often redirects cause 502s.

caroline: thanks all, leaving this thread for the bug to track. :thumbsup:
